correctness.rationale: The finite simple dumbbell \(B(a,b,d)\) with \(a,b\ge3\) and \(d\ge1\), has a+b+d-1 vertices and a+b+d edges. The incidence identity adds exactly one negative adjacency eigenvalue relative to Q(B)-2I. Exhaustive residue-by-residue congruence decomposition of each attached cycle gives balanced path modes, possible cycle-kernel zeros, and endpoint weight 1/3/-1 or a deleted endpoint; the saddle block for residue 2 is nonsingular and preserves remote couplings. The remaining ordinary weighted path is classified exactly in all cases of zero/one/two deleted endpoints and both parities of d. The signature and nullity corollaries are algebraic case analyses. A standalone independent direct rational symmetric-elimination algorithm checked all three inertia indices on 512 line-graph adjacency matrices and validated sample singular cases. No finite experiment is treated as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Disjoint-cycle dumbbells are one of the three canonical bicyclic core geometries, and a directly related 2026 line-graph inertia paper solved the other two, explicitly leaving dumbbells outside scope. Computing the complete adjacency inertia including singular parameter regimes fills this natural gap, yields exact multiplicities of the signless-Laplacian eigenvalue two, and identifies every equality configuration for the formerly conjectured line-graph signature-one bound on this class. All positive cycle and bridge lengths are covered, with no arbitrary finite cutoff or isolated normalization computation; attached trees and larger cactus classes remain outside scope.
